chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

A son of one of the companions of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) died, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) attended. When he was placed in the grave niche, his father stepped forward and threw soil upon him. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) took his hands and said: 'Do not throw soil upon him, and whoever is a close relative of his should not throw soil upon him, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the parent or one with womb relationships from throwing soil upon their deceased.'

So we said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, are you forbidding us from this alone?' He said: 'I am forbidding you from throwing soil upon your close relatives, for that causes hardness in the heart, and whoever is hard of heart is distant from his Lord.'
ai.seo_question: Why should parents not throw soil on the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical act of burial to spiritual psychology, warning that parents throwing soil may develop 'hardness of the heart' (qasawat al-qalb), a state of emotional detachment that distances one from God. This ruling is rooted in the Prophet’s prohibition and is interpreted by Shia scholars as preserving the natural tenderness of kinship, preventing the ritual from becoming a mechanical act that dulls emotional sensitivity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘A son of one of the companions of Abu Abdullahasws died. So Abu Abdullahasws attended (the funeral). So when he (the deceased) was placed in the chasm (Lahad), heasws spread soil upon him. Abu Abdullahasws grabbed with his palm and said: ‘None should spread the soil upon him, one who was a close relative of his, for Rasool-Allahsaww forbade the parent, or one with womb relationships to spread soil upon the deceased’.

So we said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Are you<sup>asws</sup> forbidding us from this (deceased) alone?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am forbidding you all from spreading the souil upon your near relatives, for that would inherit the hardness in the hearts, and the one who is hard of heart is remote from his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Ali ibn Asbat from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:

“A son of one of the companions of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, died. Abu ‘Abd Allah attended the funeral. When the deceased was placed in the grave, his father went forward to toss soil into his grave. Abu ‘Abd Allah held his hand and said, ‘You must not toss soil on him. No one of his relatives should do so. The Messenger of Allah has prohibited a father and relatives to do so.’

We asked him (the Imam), ‘O son of the Messenger of Allah, do you prohibit in this case only?’ He replied, ‘I prohibit from tossing soil in the grave of your relatives; it causes hardheartedness and those suffering from hardheartedness are away from their Lord.’”
